title: FATHER GOD, FIGHT FOR ME WHILE I REST IN YOU
text: Beloved, before we go into the depths of this word today, I want you to do something for me. Wherever you are watching this, listening to this, I want you to share this message. There is somebody in your contact list. There is somebody on your timeline. There is somebody in your family who needs to hear this word. The Holy Spirit has orchestrated this moment and you are a vessel of distribution. Share this prayer. Share this word because what God is about to release in this atmosphere is not just for you. It is for nations. It is for [music] families. It is for that person who has been fighting battles in their own strength and they are weary. Share it now in Jesus's mighty name. Now lift up your hands wherever you are. I don't care where you are seated. I don't care what time of the day or [music] night you are watching this. Lift up your hands and open your mouth and begin to worship the God of all flesh. Begin to magnify the ancient of days. Tell him, "Lord, I am weary, but you are my strength. Lord, I have been fighting, but today I learn to rest in [music] your battles." Open your mouth and worship him. Worship him in the beauty of holiness. Worship him because he's Jehovah Nissi, the Lord our banner. Worship him because he's Jehovah Sabbath, the Lord of hosts. Let worship come out of your spirit right now in the mighty name of [music] Jesus. Father, we thank you because your word says that you will perfect that which concerns us. We thank you, Lord, because your word declares that the battle is not ours but yours. We thank you because even when we are weak, you are strong. Even when we are tired, you are the everlasting God who faints not, neither is weary. Lord, as we go into this word, I pray that every ear that hears, every heart that receives will encounter a dimension of your rest that swallows up anxiety, that swallows up fear, that swallows up the weariness of warfare. Open our eyes, Lord, to see that you are the man of war. Teach us, Father, the mystery of resting while you fight. In Jesus mighty name we have prayed. Now, I want you to say this after me. Lord, teach me to rest in you while you fight for me. Say it again. Teach me to rest [music] in you while you fight for me. One more time with all your heart. Teach me to rest in you while you fight for me. You see, beloved, there is a dimension of spiritual maturity that many believers have not accessed. We have been taught to fight. We have been taught to wrestle. We have been taught to war in the realm of the spirit. And all of that is correct. Ephesians chapter 6 tells us that we wrestle not against flesh and blood, but against principalities, against powers, against the rulers of the darkness of this world, against spiritual wickedness in high places. The Bible tells us to put on the whole armor of God. We understand [music] warfare. We understand intercession. We understand engaging the enemy. But there is a place, there is a dimension, there is a realm in God where you fight by resting. There is a realm where your rest becomes your weapon. There is a realm where your confidence in God becomes the very thing that paralyzes the kingdom of darkness. Look at Exodus chapter 14. The children of Israel are standing at the Red Sea. Behind them is the most sophisticated, the most brutal, the most technological army of their time, Pharaoh and his chariots. In front of them is an impassible body of water. There is no boat. There is no bridge. There is no visible solution. And the Bible says the people began to panic. They began to murmmor against Moses. They said where there no graves in Egypt that you have brought us here to die in the wilderness. They were looking at the impossibility of their situation. [music] They were calculating with human intelligence. They were analyzing with carnal wisdom. But watch what Moses said in verse 13 and 14. He said, "Fear ye not, stand still and see the salvation of the Lord, which he will show to you today. For the Egyptians whom you have seen today, you shall see them again no more forever. The Lord shall fight for you and you shall hold your peace." Do you see that? The Lord shall fight for you and you shall hold your peace. That word hold your peace in the Hebrew carries the meaning of being silent, of being still, of resting. It means to cease from your own efforts, to cease from your own panic, to cease from your own noise. God was saying, "I need you to be quiet so I can show you who I am. I need you to stand still so I can demonstrate my power. I need you to rest so I can fight on your behalf." You see, the problem with many of us is that we don't know how to rest in God. We are so busy trying to fix things with our own hands. We are so busy trying to manipulate circumstances. We are so busy trying to orchestrate outcomes. We are so busy calling people, begging people, manipulating systems, cutting corners, trying to force doors to open. And God is saying, "If only you would be still. If only you would trust me. If only you would rest in my ability. I will show you dimensions of my power that you have never seen before." The Bible says in Psalm 46:10, "Be still and know that I am God. I will be exalted among the heathen. I will be exalted in the earth. That stillness, that rest is not passivity. It is not laziness. [music] It is not irresponsibility. It is a militant trust. It is an aggressive confidence in the ability of God. It is a spiritual posture that says, God, I have done all I know to do in the natural. I have prayed. I have fasted. I have declared your word. And now I am going to rest in the knowledge that you are fighting for me. When you rest in God, [music] you are not giving up. You are not surrendering to the enemy. You are surrendering to the superior [music] strategy of heaven. You are aligning yourself with the battle plans of the ancient of days. You are positioning yourself to watch God do what only God can do. Look at 2 Chronicles chapter 20. Jehoshaphat and the children of Judah are facing a confederacy of enemies. The children of Moab, the children of Ammon, and others coming against them. The Bible says Jehoshaphat feared and set himself to seek the Lord. He proclaimed a fast throughout all Judah. And when they gathered together, Jehoshaphat prayed a prayer that I want you to understand. He said in verse 12, "Oh our God, will you not judge them? For we have no might against this great company that comes against us, neither know we what to do, but our eyes are upon you. Did you hear that? We don't know what to do. That is not a statement of defeat. That is a statement of dependency. That is a declaration that says, God, we are not looking to our own wisdom. We are not looking to our own strength. We're not looking to our own strategy. Our eyes are upon you. And when your eyes are upon God, when your focus is on him and not on your problem, when your meditation is on his ability and not on your inability, something shifts in the realm of the spirit. [music] The Bible says the spirit of the Lord came upon Jahaziel and he stood up in the midst of the congregation and said, "Thus says the Lord unto you. Be not afraid nor dismayed by reason of this great multitude. For the battle is not yours, but God's. Tomorrow go down against them. [music] You shall not need to fight in this battle. Set yourselves, stand still, and see the salvation of the Lord with you." Did you catch that? You shall not need to fight. And what did they do? The Bible says Jehoshaphat appointed singers to go before the army singing and praising the Lord. They went out with worship. They went out with confidence. [music] They went out with rest in their spirit knowing that God had already won the battle. And the Bible says that as they began to sing and to praise, the Lord set ambushments against their enemies and their enemies destroyed themselves. Judah didn't lift a sword. They didn't shoot an arrow. They didn't engage in physical combat. They rested in the promise of God and God [music] fought for them. Now I want you to understand something. This rest, this divine rest is not based on your circumstances looking good. It is not based on your situation appearing favorable. It is based on the character [music] and the covenant faithfulness of God. You rest because you know who he is, not because you understand [music] what he's doing. You rest because his word is true, not because your feelings are settled. You rest because he has proven [music] himself faithful time and time and time again. The Bible says in Hebrews chapter 4, "There remains therefore a rest to the people of God. For he that is entered into his rest, he also has ceased from his own works [music] as God did from his." When you enter into God's rest, you cease from your own works. You stop trying to make things happen in your own strength. You stop exhausting yourself with worry and anxiety. You stop losing sleep over what only God can fix. You enter into a place of Sabbath rest where you trust God completely. Now, let me tell you what happens in the spirit realm. When you rest in God, when you rest, you are making a prophetic declaration to the kingdom of darkness that you are not afraid. When you rest, you are announcing to principalities and powers that your confidence is not in what you see but in what God has spoken. When you rest, you are frustrating the strategy of the enemy because his entire warfare against [music] you is designed to make you panic, to make you anxious, to make you take matters into your own hands and make mistakes. Satan knows that when you are anxious, when you are fearful, when you are operating in panic, you make wrong decisions. You say things you shouldn't say. You do things you shouldn't do. You align yourself with people you shouldn't align yourself with. But when you are resting in God, when you are still when you are peaceful, you operate in divine wisdom. You hear the voice of God clearly. You discern the strategy of heaven accurately. You move with precision and authority. Isaiah 30:15 says, "For thus says the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel, in returning and rest shall you be saved. In quietness and in confidence shall be your strength. Do you hear that? In quietness and in confidence shall be your strength. Your strength is not in how loud you can shout. Your strength is not in how much you can worry. Your strength is not in how many people you can call. Your strength is in your quiet confidence in God. I hear the Lord saying to somebody right now, the battle you are fighting, I have already won it. The situation you are stressing over, I have already resolved it. The door you are trying to force open, I have already prepared it. But you need to rest. You need to stop striving. You need to stop manipulating. You need to stop operating in fear. Rest in me and watch me fight for you. There are battles that will never be won by your strength. There are enemies that will never be defeated by your wisdom. There are doors that will never open by your connections. There are some things that require the direct intervention of the God of all flesh. And the only way to access that divine intervention is to rest, to [music] trust, to surrender to his superior strategy. Let me take you to another dimension. In the book of Isaiah chapter 37, King Hezekiah is facing an impossible situation. The Assyrian army led by Sakaribb has surrounded Jerusalem. Rapshake, the mouthpiece of the Assyrian king, stands at the gates mocking God, mocking Hezekiah, telling the people that no God of any nation has been able to deliver them from the hand of Assyria. So, how can the God of Israel deliver them? He blasphemes the name of God. He ridicules the faith of God's people. Now, Hezekiah could have panicked. He could have tried to negotiate. He could have tried to form political alliances. He could have tried to gather his own military strength. But watch what [music] Hezekiah did. The Bible says he took the letter from the messengers. He went into the house of the Lord and he spread it before the Lord. He didn't take it to the United Nations. He didn't take it to his council of adviserss. He took it to God and he prayed a prayer that moved heaven. He said, "Oh Lord of hosts, God of Israel that dwells between the cherubim. You are the God, even you alone of all the kingdoms of the earth. You have made heaven and earth. Incline your ear, O Lord, and hear. Open your eyes, oh Lord, and see, and hear all the words of senicaribb which are sent to reproach the living God." Now therefore, oh Lord our God, save us from his hand, that all the kingdoms of the earth may know that you are the Lord, even you only. And watch what God did. The Bible says that night the angel of the Lord went forth and smokeote in the camp of the Assyrians 185,000 men. One angel, one night. And when they arose early in the morning, behold, they were all dead corpses. Hezekiah didn't lift a sword. The army of Judah didn't engage in battle. God fought for them while they rested in his [music] covenant. This is what I'm trying to show you. When you rest in God, you are not passive. You are positioning yourself for divine intervention. You are creating room for God to move. You are stepping aside so that God can step in. And when God steps in, no [music] enemy can stand. When God steps in, no mountain can remain. When God steps in, the impossible becomes possible. Now, somebody might say, "But Apostle, doesn't the Bible tell us to fight the good fight of faith? Doesn't the Bible tell us to resist the devil and he will flee from us? Doesn't the Bible tell us to war a good warfare?" Absolutely. But you need to understand the difference between waring in your own strength and waring in God's strength. You need to understand the difference between fighting in panic and fighting in rest. You need to understand the difference between warfare that exhausts you and warfare [music] that strengthens you. When you fight from a place of rest, you fight from victory, not for victory. You are not trying to defeat an enemy that is already defeated. You are enforcing [music] the victory that Jesus already won on the cross. You are not begging God to intervene. You are declaring what God has already said. You are not hoping that maybe God will help you. You are confident that God is fighting for you. That is a declaration of absolute confidence. If God, the creator of heaven and earth, the one who spoke and worlds came into existence, the one who holds the breath of every living thing in his hands, the one who rules over principalities and powers. If this God is for you, then it doesn't matter who is against you. It doesn't matter how powerful your enemy appears to be. It doesn't matter how impossible your situation looks. God is fighting for you. I want to pray right now. Wherever you are, lift up your hands. Father, in the mighty name of Jesus, I speak rest into weary spirits right now. I speak peace into troubled hearts. I speak confidence [music] into believers who have been fighting battles in their own strength and have grown weary. Lord, teach them. Teach us to rest in you. Teach us to trust your ability more than we trust our own efforts. Teach us to lean on your understanding more than we lean on our own intelligence. Father, I decree that every battle that your children are facing right now, you are stepping into those battles. You are fighting for them. You are moving on their behalf. Lord, let them see your salvation. Let them see your deliverance. [music] Let them see your power manifested in ways that leave no doubt that you are God in Jesus's mighty name. Now I want to take you to the New Testament in the Gospel of Mark chapter 4. Jesus and his disciples are in a boat crossing over to the other side of the sea. The Bible says a great storm arose and the waves were beaten into the ship so that the ship was filling with water. The disciples many of whom were experienced fishermen were panicking. They were terrified. They were convinced they were going to die. And where was Jesus? The Bible says he was in the hinder part of the ship, asleep on a pillow. Can you imagine that? There is a storm threatening to sink the boat. Water is pouring in. Experienced sailors are panicking and Jesus is sleeping. Not because he didn't care. Not because he was irresponsible, but because he was resting in the absolute knowledge that no storm, no wind, no wave, no circumstance could override the purpose and [music] the plan of God for his life. The disciples woke him up and said, "Master, hear us thou not that we perish." And Jesus arose and rebuked the wind and said to the sea, "Peace, be still." And the wind ceased. And there was a great calm. Then he turned to his disciples and said, "Why are you so fearful? How is it that you have no faith?" You see, Jesus was teaching them something profound. He was teaching them that faith and rest are connected. When you truly have faith in God, you can rest in [music] the midst of the storm. When you truly believe that God is in control, you can sleep when others are panicking. When you truly know that God's purposes for your life cannot be aborted by any storm, any attack, any opposition, you can have peace in the midst of chaos. The reason many of us cannot rest is because our faith is in our own ability to control the situation. We think that if we don't stay awake, if we don't worry, if we don't keep trying to [music] fix things, everything will fall apart. But God is saying, I need you to trust me. I need you to believe that I'm bigger than your storm. I need you to know that I'm fighting for you even when you are sleeping. There is a dimension of rest that is actually spiritual warfare. When you refuse to panic in the face of opposition, you are worrying. When you refuse to be moved by what you see and you stand on what God has said, you are worrying. When you choose peace over anxiety, rest over striving, [music] faith over fear, you are engaging in the most powerful form of spiritual warfare because you are demonstrating that your confidence is in God and not in circumstances. Philippians 4:6-7 says, "Be careful for nothing, but in everything by prayer and supplication with thanksgiving, let your requests be made known unto God. And the peace of God which passes all understanding shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus." That peace that passes understanding is supernatural rest. It doesn't make sense to the natural mind. It doesn't make sense to people who are looking at your situation, but when you have the peace of God guarding your heart, you can rest in the midst of the battle. Number three, pray in the spirit. Romans 8:26 says, "Likewise, the spirit also helps our infirmities. For we know not what we should pray for as we ought, but the spirit itself makes intercession for us with groanings [music] which cannot be uttered." When you don't know what to pray, when the battle is confusing, when you can't articulate what you need, pray in the spirit. Let the Holy Spirit intercede through you. Let him pray the perfect will of God over your situation. And as you pray in the spirit, you will find rest because you know that the Holy Spirit knows exactly what needs to happen and he's praying it through you. Number four, surround yourself with the right people. The Bible says in Proverbs 13:20, "He that walks with wise men shall be wise, but [music] a companion of fools shall be destroyed." You cannot rest in God if you are surrounded by people who speak fear, doubt, and unbelief into your life. You need to surround yourself with people of faith, people who will remind you of God's [music] promises, people who will encourage you to trust God, people who will war with you in the spirit. Number five, obey God's instructions completely. Partial obedience is disobedience. When God gives you an instruction, obey it fully, immediately, and completely. Don't add to it. Don't subtract from it. Don't delay it. Don't modify it. Just obey it. And when you obey God, you position yourself for his blessing, his protection, and his intervention. Now, let me pray a militant prayer. If you are ready to enter into this rest, if you are tired of fighting in your own strength, if you are ready to watch God fight for you, lift up your hands right now and repeat this prayer after me. Father, in the name of Jesus, I come before your throne of grace. Lord, I confess that I have been weary. I've been fighting battles in my own strength and I am exhausted. Today, I choose to rest in you. I choose to trust your [music] ability more than my own efforts. Lord, I surrender every battle to you. I surrender every situation to you. I surrender [music] every concern to you. Fight for me, Lord. Move on my behalf. Intervene in my circumstances. Show me your salvation. Show me your power. Show me your glory. Every enemy that has risen against me, I declare that they are defeated because you are fighting for me. Every obstacle in my path, I declare that it is removed because you are making a way for me. Every door that needs to open, I declare that it is open because you are my door opener. Lord, teach me to rest in you. Teach me to trust you completely. Teach me to walk in faith [music] and not in fear. I receive your peace that passes understanding. I receive your rest that swallows up anxiety. I receive your strength that perfects itself in my weakness. In Jesus mighty name I have prayed. Amen. Now begin to thank him. Begin to worship him. Begin to magnify his name. Tell him Lord I trust you. Lord I rest in you. Lord I know that you are fighting for me. Let worship come out of your spirit. Let thanksgiving [music] flow from your heart because when you worship, you are sealing your faith. When you thank him before you see the manifestation, you are declaring that his [music] word is true and his promises are yes and amen. The Bible says in 1 Peter 5:7, "Casting all your care upon him, for he cares for you." Cast your cares on him. That word cast means to throw it, to haul it, to get it away from you. Stop carrying burdens that God never told you to carry. Stop holding on to worries that are blocking your rest. Cast it all on him. He cares for you. He's concerned about everything that concerns you. Nothing is too small for his attention. Nothing is too big for his power. I hear the Lord saying, "The season of striving is over. The season of rest has begun. I am fighting for you. I am moving on your behalf. I am opening doors that no man can shut. I am making ways where there seems to be no way. Trust me, rest in me and watch me do what only I can do. Beloved, this is not just a message. This is an invitation into a lifestyle. [music] A lifestyle of resting in God while he fights for you. A lifestyle of trusting him completely. A lifestyle [music] of walking in faith and not in fear. a lifestyle where your peace becomes your testimony and your rest becomes your weapon. Wherever you are, I release the grace to rest upon you in the mighty name of [music] Jesus. I speak supernatural peace into your spirit. I speak divine confidence into your heart. I speak holy boldness into your mind. You will not be moved by what you see. You will not be shaken by what you hear. You will not be intimidated by the size of your enemy. because you know that the God who fights for you is greater than any enemy that fight against you in Jesus mighty name.
